title: add provenance-backed metadata enricher and performance-stamp publisher
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: When models are onboarded we lack a compact, auditable performance signature attached to the model metadata that can be consumed by release note automation and ops tooling. This PR introduces a provenance-backed metadata enricher that synthesizes canonical metadata fields (fingerprint, hardware-affinity hints, sample-derived latency/p90/cost stamps) and a separate performance-stamp publisher that emits a small, versioned artifact used by the changelog/autodraft hook to populate 'performance notes' in release drafts. Scope: 1) onboarding enricher service (onboard/enricher) that runs post-ingest to compute and attach a performance signature and provenance ledger entry; 2) publisher service (publisher/stamp_publisher) that signs and stores a compact JSON stamp in model artifacts storage and emits an event for release automation; 3) small CLI hook (hooks/autodraft_publisher) consumed by the changelog synthesizer to include the stamp in draft release notes; 4) unit + integration tests and docs. Design notes: the enricher uses existing sampling harness (ingest/probes) and a deterministic fingerprinting algorithm to ensure stamps are reproducible; the publisher attaches a provenance token and KMS-wrapped signature (optional via feature flag) so downstream workflows can assert authenticity. Backwards compatibility: stamps are optional metadata keys and will not block existing onboards. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout initially on the canary intake pipeline, then enabled by default after 2 weeks of telemetry. Checklist: - [x] core enricher implementation - [x] publisher that writes signed stamp to blobstore - [x] changelog hook to read stamps and synthesize a performance blurb - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] docs and runbook entry - [x] feature-flag gating and migration path Tests: added deterministic unit tests for fingerprinting and a small integration test that simulates probe ingestion and stamp emission. Security: signing flow is pluggable; by default uses a development key if KMS is not configured. Impact: improves fidelity of automated release notes and provides a verifiable performance artifact for platform teams. See related Linear items ENG-1428 and ENG-1492 for telemetry and rollout milestones.
